meaning.zh:
“无稽之谈” 或 “荒诞不经的故事”。

这个短语的确切起源存在争议，一种观点认为它源自于 17 世纪英国的一家名为"公鸡和公牛"的客栈，是一个关于人们酒后编造虚假、荒诞故事的传说。另一种说法是，这个短语即从故事本身的荒谬与无稽角度出发。无论如何，这个短语现在用来形容那些编出来的，令人难以置信的故事。
meaning.en: The exact origin of this phrase is debated; one theory is that it originates from a 17th-century inn in England named "Cock and Bull," where people purportedly told exaggerated and fanciful tales. Another theory suggests the phrase simply refers to the absurd and unbelievable nature of such stories. Nowadays, this idiom is used to describe fabricated and highly improbable stories.

lines.en: He told me a real *cock-and-bull story* about why he was late.
lines.zh: 他给我编了一个无稽之谈来解释他为什么迟到。

lines.en: Don’t believe his *cock-and-bull story*; he’s just trying to cover up his mistake.
lines.zh: 别相信他的荒诞故事，他只是在掩盖他的错误。

lines.en: That was the most ridiculous *cock-and-bull story* I've ever heard.
lines.zh: 那是我听过的最荒谬的无稽之谈。
